title: The 10 Best Air Compressors
subtitle: Pancake, portable and upright shop compressors for nailers, tires and air tools, ranked from live Amazon data.
intro: A shop air compressor stores air in a tank so it can run nail guns, inflate tires, blow off parts and power air tools. The number that matters most is airflow (CFM at 90 PSI): small pancakes run brad and finish nailers, and bigger tanks with more CFM keep up with framing nailers, impact wrenches and spray guns. We ranked 10 best-sellers on rating, review volume and features (4+ CFM, 150+ PSI, quiet operation, wheels and an accessory kit). They run from about $136 for a 4.8-gallon unit to $380 for a 29-gallon upright. Tire inflators are left out.
data_source: Amazon product listings on the data_captured date. Prices, ratings and review counts change daily; check the listing before relying on a number.

avoid.name: MZB 13.2 Gallon Ultra Quiet Air Compressor, 115PSI, Oil Free
avoid.flag: Claims 14.83 CFM and 3 HP from a 110V outlet
avoid.verdict: A 13-gallon compressor sold on an airflow figure no 110V compressor can deliver. The VEVOR 13-gallon costs about $16 more, publishes a believable 4.6 SCFM, and is rated 66 dB.
reasons: The spec table claims 14.83 CFM and 3 HP. The 2.5 HP, 29-gallon Klutch on this page delivers 5.1 SCFM on the same household power; a standard 120V circuit can't run a motor that makes three times that.
The bullet points promise "high airflow" but never give a CFM figure at 90 PSI, the number that tells you which tools it can run.
It's rated 5.0 stars, the lowest of any compressor we considered, and its 115 PSI maximum is lower than every pick here.

buyers_guide.q: What size compressor do I need?
buyers_guide.a: Match airflow (CFM at 90 PSI) to your hungriest tool. Brad and finish nailers need under 1 CFM, so any pancake works. Framing nailers want 2 to 4 CFM; impact wrenches, sanders and spray guns want 4 CFM or more, and a bigger tank so the motor isn't running constantly.

buyers_guide.q: What's the difference between a pancake, hot dog and upright?
buyers_guide.a: Those describe the tank shape. Pancakes are flat and stable, hot dogs are small horizontal cylinders, and uprights stand vertically on wheels to save floor space. Shape matters less than tank size and CFM.
Most air tools run at 90 PSI. A higher maximum (150 to 200 PSI) stores more air in the same tank, so you get more nails between motor cycles. It doesn't make tools more powerful.
Every pick here is oil-free: no oil to check or change, and clean air for painting. Oil-lubricated compressors run quieter and last longer in daily shop use, but they cost more and need maintenance.

Standard pancake compressors are loud, often 80 dB or more. Quiet models with induction motors run around 66 to 70 dB, about the level of a conversation, which matters in an attached garage or basement.
